clue.text: Free to accept an honour in return for being gallant

indicators.note: a word that accepts something takes it in, so the honour and its article go inside the word for free
a return goes back the way it came, so the whole built word is read from right to left

blocks.note: to rid is to free, as in rid of pests
taken as written
the Order of the British Empire, a British honour

explanation.surface: Someone is freed in exchange for accepting an honour for gallantry.
explanation.walkthrough: RID holds AN OBE to make RIANOBED, which read backwards is DEBONAIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Debonair describes a man who is suave, charming and courteous, the manner of a dashing gentleman.

clue.text: Take time to follow sound of the sea mew

indicators.note: only the sound of the word that follows is wanted, so it becomes the letter it is pronounced like

blocks.note: sea is pronounced like the letter C
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: An instruction to wait and follow the cry of a seagull.
explanation.walkthrough: The sea mew looks like a gull, but mew stands alone: a mew is a cage for hawks, as in the royal mews.
explanation.definitionFit: A mew is an enclosure where falconers kept hawks while moulting, so it is a kind of cage.

clue.text: Place where dangerous plot may be hatched

definitions.text: Place where dangerous plot may be hatched

blocks.clueFragment: Place where dangerous plot may be hatched
blocks.note: surface reading: a den where conspirators devise a sinister scheme
setter's reading: a plot of ground, a garden bed warmed so that things grow and hatch

explanation.walkthrough: The word for a breeding ground of trouble is also literally a heated garden bed, so plot works both ways.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotbed is a place encouraging rapid growth of something undesirable, such as crime or conspiracy.

clue.text: Immediately north is which town?

blocks.note: presto means at once, as in hey presto
N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: A quiz question asking which town lies directly to the north.
explanation.walkthrough: PRESTON is a town in Lancashire, in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Preston is a Lancashire town, granted city status in 2002, in north-west England.

clue.text: Apt to change leader? Quite the contrary!

indicators.note: changing the leader means swapping the first letter of the word for another

blocks.note: apposite means apt or well suited

explanation.surface: Someone liable to switch leaders, met with an exclamation of contradiction.
explanation.walkthrough: APPOSITE has its first letter A replaced by O.
explanation.definitionFit: Quite the contrary is said when the reverse is true, which is exactly the opposite.

clue.text: Currently engaged in training

blocks.note: first meaning: actively working in a profession, as a doctor or lawyer does
second meaning: rehearsing a skill repeatedly to improve it

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one phrase about someone busy training, but splits into two senses of the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: A practising solicitor currently follows the profession, and someone practising scales is drilling to improve.

clue.text: State a boy's name backwards

indicators.note: going backwards means the letters built from the rest are read from the end

blocks.note: taken as written
a boy's name, short for David
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: An instruction to say a boy's name in reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like the verb say, but it is the definition: a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: Nevada is one of the fifty United States, home of Las Vegas.

clue.text: Join the party or thrash

blocks.note: to be with or of something is to belong to it
the British Labour Party

explanation.surface: An ultimatum: sign up to the party or face a beating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Be Labour' means be a member of the Labour Party, one of Britain's two main political parties.
explanation.definitionFit: To belabour someone is to beat or attack them vigorously, an old verb for thrashing.

clue.text: Uncontaminated drug extract

blocks.note: pure means free from contamination
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A clean, untainted extract of some medicinal drug.
explanation.definitionFit: A purée is pulp pressed and sieved from fruit or vegetables, so it is something extracted from them.

clue.text: Take exercise? Stuff it!

blocks.note: to do a class is to take it
physical education, the school exercise lesson

explanation.surface: Someone is told to go and exercise, and replies rudely: stuff it!
explanation.walkthrough: Stuff it looks like a rude retort, but stuff is a noun: dope is slang for drugs or information.
explanation.definitionFit: Dope is slang for drugs, just as stuff is a casual word for any substance, especially narcotics.

clue.text: Sea creature brought to port in hold

blocks.note: Boston is a port in Massachusetts and in Lincolnshire
a crab is a sea creature, here placed after the port

explanation.surface: A crab caught and carried into harbour in the ship's hold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hold' looks like the ship's cargo space, but it is a wrestling grip.
explanation.definitionFit: A Boston crab is a wrestling submission grip, bending the opponent's legs back while they lie face down.

clue.text: Demolished, say? Quite the opposite!

indicators.note: say asks for the word as spoken, so its sound leads to a different spelling

blocks.note: razed means demolished, flattened to the ground

explanation.surface: Was it knocked down? No, the reverse!
explanation.walkthrough: Razed and raised sound the same yet mean opposites: one pulls down, the other puts up.
explanation.definitionFit: Raised means built up or erected, the contrary of being knocked down to the ground.

clue.text: Works on paper

blocks.note: surface reading: drawings or writings, or someone labouring at a desk
setter's reading: musical compositions, printed out as scores

explanation.walkthrough: Works suggests labour or artwork; here it means musical works, printed for players to read.
explanation.definitionFit: Printed scores for performers are compositions in written form on loose leaves.

clue.text: Master said to have taken a single?

definitions.text: said to have taken a single?

blocks.note: first meaning: the master copy from which reproductions are made

blocks.clueFragment: said to have taken a single?
blocks.note: second meaning: in Christian doctrine everyone is said to have taken on one inherited sin, called by this word

explanation.walkthrough: The second half reads like cricket, but alludes to original sin, the single sin all are said to bear from Adam.
explanation.definitionFit: An original is the first version, the master from which copies are made; original sin is that inherited single fault.

clue.text: Ground, home to Southern League side

indicators.note: a place that is home to something houses it, so one word sits inside the other

blocks.note: an arena is a sports ground
S is the abbreviation for southern
L is the abbreviation for league

explanation.surface: A stadium that hosts a team from a southern football league.
explanation.walkthrough: ARENA holds S, then L follows. Arsenal is a London football club, in the south of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Arsenal is a famous English football team, and a side is a sports team.

clue.text: Is, oddly, love to matter nothing to Cupid?

indicators.note: doing something oddly means in a strange way, so the letters fall into an unusual order

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
taken as written
nothing is zero, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A whimsical question: does it strangely matter nothing to the god of love?
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'to' joins the pieces; the second introduces the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An amoretto is a little cherub of love in Italian art, a figure of the god of desire.

clue.text: Stage in development of a plant

indicators.note: something in development is being reshaped, so the letters are worked into a new form

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A phase in the growth of some plant.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as botany, so 'stage in' passes as part of the phrase rather than the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Genista is the broom genus, a yellow-flowered shrub of the pea family.

clue.text: In the stretch between wings, a sole player

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so the single letter goes within the stretch

blocks.note: taken as written
a wingspan is the stretch from tip to tip
a single one, the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Alone between the stage wings, a single actor performs.
explanation.walkthrough: Wings suggests the theatre, but here it is the span of a bird's wings.
explanation.definitionFit: A thespian is an actor, named after Thespis, the legendary first actor of ancient Greece.

clue.text: Whisper circulating about daughter's size

indicators.note: to circulate about something is to go around it, so one word surrounds the other

blocks.note: a breath is a faint whisper, as in a breath of scandal
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: Gossip going round about how big someone's daughter is.
explanation.definitionFit: Breadth is width, a dimension that measures how large something is from side to side.

clue.text: A club free-for-all turned into a shambles

indicators.note: something turned faces the other way, so the free-for-all word is read backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
a bat is a club used to strike a ball
a riot is a disorderly free-for-all

explanation.surface: A brawl at a nightclub that descends into chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: Shambles looks like a mess, but its old meaning is a slaughterhouse, as in the Shambles street in York.
explanation.definitionFit: A shambles was originally a meat market or slaughterhouse, which is what an abattoir is.

clue.text: Girl's garment to hide the rear?

indicators.note: to hide something is to cover it up, so the garment closes around the other word

blocks.note: a bra is an undergarment
the end is the rear

explanation.surface: A cheeky question about a girl's garment meant to cover her bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: The garment covering the rear suggests knickers, but it is a bra wrapped around END.
explanation.definitionFit: Brenda is a female given name, so it can stand for a girl in crossword terms.

clue.text: Good artist all-round - one with drawing ability

indicators.note: going all round something encloses it, so the artist wraps the other letter

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
Édouard Manet, French painter

explanation.surface: A versatile artist who is also a skilled draughtsman.
explanation.walkthrough: Drawing ability suggests sketching, but it means the power to draw things towards it.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnet attracts iron, pulling it closer, so it has the power of attraction.

clue.text: Girl in outrageous dress - a frenzied female

indicators.note: a girl in a dress is wearing it, so her name sits inside the other word

blocks.note: mad means wild or outrageous
Ena is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl in a shocking outfit behaving like a wild woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Ena Sharples was a famous character in the British soap Coronation Street, so ENA is a common crossword girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Maenads were the wild female followers of Dionysus, and the word now means any woman in a frenzy.

clue.text: To rally, poorly creature's given exercise for the heart

indicators.note: something poorly is unwell and out of shape, so the creature's letters are muddled
the heart is the middle, so the exercise goes into the centre of the jumbled word

blocks.note: taken as written
physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: A sick animal is put on cardio exercise to help it rally.
explanation.walkthrough: Exercise for the heart sounds like cardio, but it says put PE into the middle of the rearranged creature.
explanation.definitionFit: To recuperate is to recover health and strength, as a patient rallies after illness.

clue.text: Manage firm with record turnover

indicators.note: a turnover flips something over, so the record is read backwards

blocks.note: Co is the abbreviation for company
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: Running a business that has a record annual turnover.
explanation.walkthrough: Turnover reads as business revenue, but it signals flipping the record.
explanation.definitionFit: To cope is to deal successfully with something difficult, to get by and manage.

clue.text: US barque coming into port

blocks.note: first meaning: barque is spelt bark in America, and this is the bark of a particular oak
second meaning: a harbour city in the south of Ireland

explanation.surface: An American sailing ship arriving in harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: The US ship is a pun: barque spelt the American way is bark, and the answer is tree bark.
explanation.definitionFit: Cork is the spongy outer bark of the cork oak, and also a major Irish seaport.

clue.text: Vein in one foot attended to by medic

blocks.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor
I is the Roman numeral one
ft is the abbreviation for foot

explanation.surface: A doctor treats a patient's vein in one foot.
explanation.walkthrough: Vein looks medical, but it means the general tenor or gist of something, as in speaking in a light vein.
explanation.definitionFit: The drift of an argument is its general meaning or tenor, which is also what vein can mean.

clue.text: When to eat baker's creation?

indicators.note: a creation is something newly made, so the letters are shaped into a new word

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Asking when one should tuck into a cake the baker has made.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition while its words eat and baker are reworked; the 's just joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea break is a short pause from work for a drink and a snack, when people have cake.
